chunks: 212 - And Zurarah said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “Will you not inform me from where you knew and said that wiping is on part of the head and part of the two feet?”
So he smiled and said: “O Zurarah, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said it, and the Book from Allah was revealed with it, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:”
So we knew that the whole face should be washed. Then He said:
“And your hands up to the elbows.”
So He joined the two hands up to the elbows with the face, and we knew that they should be washed up to the elbows. Then He separated the speech and said:

So we knew, when He said “with your heads,” that wiping is on part of the head because of the letter bāʾ. Then He joined the two feet to the head just as He had joined the two hands to the face, and He said:
“And your feet up to the ankles.”
So we knew, when He joined them to the head, that wiping is upon part of them. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم explained that to the people, but they neglected it. Then He said:
“Then if you do not find water, perform tayammum with clean earth, and wipe your faces.”
So when He lifted wudu from the one who did not find water, He established part of the washing as wiping, because He said, “with your faces.” Then He joined to it:
Meaning: from that tayammum, because He knew that all of that would not pass over the face, since some of that earth adheres to part of the palm and does not adhere to part of it. Then Allah said:
“Allah does not intend to place upon you any hardship.”

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, the dry ablution performed when water is unavailable
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, of which only part is wiped in this ruling
key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the two feet, linked to the ruling of wiping
key_terms.الْكِتَابُ: the revealed Book of Allah, cited as proof for the ruling
key_terms.الْمَسْحَ: wiping as the prescribed ritual act in wudu and tayammum
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification with water
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship or constraint, which Allah does not intend for people in the law

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام derive wiping part of the head and feet in wudu from the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic basis for wiping part of the head and feet in wudu and for wiping in tayammum. Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام derives the rulings from the wording and structure of the verse, and states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم explained this to the people. It also emphasizes that the divine law is not intended to impose hardship.
